pinned_source.finding: KERN_PROC_PID selects sysdoproc_filt_KERN_PROC_PID; uidcheck/ruidcheck remain zero for this selector. sysdoproc_callback zeroes and fills the selected structure. proc_iterate includes PROC_ALLPROCLIST and PROC_ZOMBPROCLIST. A data-buffer query with no selected record returns zero consumed length, not an identity. This is a targeted API even though the kernel's internal implementation walks lists; the prototype does not request or receive a global enumeration.

fill_user64_externproc assigns p_starttime.tv_sec/usec directly from p->p_start before other fields, and assigns p_stat and PID. No full-BSD per-target UID gate surrounds these birth assignments in this published handler. fill_user64_proc invokes that function.

Full BSD pbi_start_tvsec/usec are assigned from the same p->p_start source. This supports testing equality to the repository's unchanged OwnedProcess.identity start_seconds/start_subseconds; it does not imply cross-user full-BSD permission.

Source explicitly calls these well-known kern.proc sysctls SPI, not intended for non-system user applications, while preserving binary compatibility. Public SDK declarations are NOT a supported stable application-ABI promise.
Global sysctl dispatch calls mac_system_check_sysctlbyname for user requests and propagates its error. Absence of the full-BSD UID gate does not establish unrestricted deployed access.

Nonzero arg for SHORTBSD requests zombie lookup after proc_find misses. Normal non-extended proc_pidinfo uses no extended birth/version comparison. If live and zombie lookup both miss, ESRCH is returned. SHORTBSD and PATHINFO select NO_CHECK_SAME_USER, but still run proc_security_policy. Exact size/PID checks remain essential.
proc_security_policy calls MAC before optional credential-UID checks. A same-owner positive/negative fixture cannot establish every policy module's behavior or all foreign-owner access.
PATHINFO ESRCH also covers absent/recycled text vnode and unmount conditions, not only absent PID. PATHINFO does not itself request zombie lookup. It is never sufficient for prototype absence.
proc_pidpath returns strlen(buffer) on syscall success and zero with errno on failure. Bridge captures errno immediately, before the second sysctl query.

design.queries: Exactly CTL_KERN/KERN_PROC/KERN_PROC_PID for an owned spawned PID; proc_pidpath of that retained PID; second identical metadata read; exact PROC_PIDT_SHORTBSDINFO(arg=1). No KERN_PROCARGS, argv/env, global enumeration, UID narrowing, or foreign-PID CLI input.
design.kernel_layout: All kernel layout and sizeof operations are in sdk_metadata.c using installed SDK struct kinfo_proc and struct proc_bsdshortinfo. The Rust repr(C) arrays are only our own transfer record, with a size handshake before collection and SDK compile-time assertions for its path capacity, errno constants and state values.
design.positive_reads: Validate sysctl status, exact returned sizeof, PID, 0 < start_seconds <= current wall-clock seconds, 0 <= microseconds < 1000000, state range, before/after birth equality and equality to existing OwnedProcess.identity. Require complete absolute non-parent-component path and component-wise Path.starts_with. No path-only or UID-only match.
design.absence: Zero/filtered metadata is not absence. PATHINFO zero/ESRCH is not absence. Only a later exact non-extended SHORTBSD(arg=1) missing-live-and-zombie result permits AbsentAtShortLookup after rejecting denied, malformed and mismatched-birth reads. This label is a bounded source-conditional observation, not cross-user native admission authority. A found live/zombie with absent path remains unavailable. Global/deployed-policy uncertainty remains even for source-backed error interpretations.
design.sticky_errors: Any observed EPERM/EACCES from either metadata read, PATHINFO or SHORTBSD remains Unavailable, even if a later read says missing. Other sysctl errors, sizes/PIDs/starttimes/state failures, malformed path and mismatched expected/before/after birth are also unavailable and are not healed by later absence.
design.no_new_control: Prototype classification is pure and owns no signal API. Fixture controls are exclusively the unchanged production OwnedProcess returned by spawn_with_deadline. Synthetic modified birth records are passed only to pure classify, never to observe/signal/settle.
design.observed_and_synthetic: receipt.txt prefixes real ABI cases with observed/real_zombie_kinfo and synthetic decisions with synthetic. Synthetic metadata/error/race tests do not claim the kernel produced those errors or a real PID reuse occurred.

cleanup_plan.fixture_finiteness: Each C fixture exits after at most 5 seconds of its monotonic loop or its owner's release file; it never forks or opens sockets. This is not a hard deadline for a kernel-stalled syscall.
cleanup_plan.spawn_bound: 2 seconds, fixture-only, not a production observation budget change.
cleanup_plan.observation_bound: 500 milliseconds measured around the four direct read calls; overrun is unavailable. No helper, retry, budget extension or cancellation guarantee is introduced.
cleanup_plan.owner_cleanup_bound: 8 seconds absolute deadline enrolled before each fixture spawn, never reset; 100 ms TERM grace inside existing OwnedProcess.settle. This is separate fixture-owner cleanup authority, not native/service authority.
cleanup_plan.retention: Each returned OwnedProcess is pushed into the harness before identity queries, receipt writing or assertions. Known ProcessIdentity is retained before assertions. Catch-unwind wraps the real scenario; cleanup_all runs regardless of returned error or unwind. Settlements, including failure, remain stored and are written privately. Unexpected receipt/cleanup errors fail the run.
cleanup_plan.strictness: Completion requires the unchanged OwnedProcess Settlement.complete, not only leader_reaped/group_absent. Any NOTE_FORK or sticky ownership failure remains incomplete. Program success additionally requires all final settlements to be complete. It never clears historical helper 38672 uncertainty or sends post-reap controls.
cleanup_plan.no_op: Repeated settle after a successful settlement invokes the existing cached result branch in process_scope.rs:1238-1239. The runner compares retained/cached settlement receipts; this is not renewed cleanup authority.
cleanup_plan.limits: SIGKILL, abort, machine failure or a permanently blocked kernel call can prevent in-process exception cleanup. Do not erase incomplete receipts or infer descendant absence from known-group disappearance. Parent retains artifacts for diagnosis and does not extend expired authority.
